conf.description: F5 BIG-IP ASM attack/anomaly event log, CEF profile: separate branch from the request-log CEF pipeline because the same csN/cnN slots carry different fields here (cs4=attack_status not attack_type, cn1=detection_average not response_code)

conf.comment: F5 BIG-IP ASM attack/anomaly event log (brute-force, IP enforcer, web scraping, session anomaly), CEF profile. Shares the CEF envelope with the request log but reuses cs4/cn1/cn2/cs5/cs1/cs6/cn3 for different fields, so this is a separate branch, not the request-log pipeline reused: cs4 is attack_status here, not attack_type, and cn1 is detection_average, not response_code. Every csN/cnN is resolved through its paired *Label rather than positionally, per recommendations.direct.cribl.

functions.description: why this pipeline is shaped this way
Split the CEF header into its 8 pipe-delimited fields; everything after the 7th pipe is the extension key=value string
Extract the space-delimited CEF extension dictionary (src, dst, csN/cnN and their csNLabel/cnNLabel pairs, etc.)
batch rename every status:mapped field with no transform

implement every partial/unmapped transform: csN/cnN resolved via their paired *Label (this dataset's mapping, distinct from the request log's reuse of the same slots), act/outcome direction identical to the request-log route, then drop intermediate parse artifacts
CEF rt is BIG-IP local time with no zone/offset (per-device tz unresolved - recorded as a gap); write to _time per platform constraint 1, never @timestamp
tag the dataset, hyphen-free per platform constraint 5
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
